## Natural history notes

A tiny, active songbird characterized by olive-gray upperparts, pale underparts, bold white eye ring, white wing bars, and a small red crown patch that is usually hidden except when excited. In Florida, it is mostly a winter visitor found in hammocks, pine forests, cypress swamps, mangroves, forest edges, parks, yards, and other wooded or shrubby habitats. It feeds mainly on tiny insects, spiders, and other small arthropods, foraging quickly among leaves, twigs, and branches and often flicking its wings as it moves.
